# Kobbopay — LLM / AI crawler guidance (pay.kobbex.com)

## Product definition (bounded)

Kobbopay is API-first B2B crypto payment infrastructure: server-created payments, explicit payment lifecycle semantics, signed webhooks, and merchant operations. Access requires merchant approval; enabled networks and assets are selected rails configured per environment—not universal coverage.

## Playbooks index (operational procedures)

Hub: https://pay.kobbex.com/playbooks

- merchant-onboarding-rollout: Staged merchant rollout with lifecycle gates and webhook readiness.
- webhook-secret-rotation: Dual-secret rotation without dropping verified events.
- settlement-operations-checklist: Daily settlement checkpoint review and drift signals.
- reconciliation-close-procedure: Period-close reconciliation with evidence collection and freeze rules.
- treasury-recognition-procedure: Books-ready recognition gates separate from detection.
- delayed-settlement-recovery: Recover stuck payments using checkpoints—not commerce rewrites.
- duplicate-payment-investigation: Idempotency-aware duplicate and replay investigation.
- underpayment-overpayment-handling: Amount variance triage with exception queue ownership.
- exception-queue-triage: Classify, route, and resolve operational exceptions with audit trail.
- provider-outage-response: Bounded degradation during provider or rail outages.
- confirmation-policy-escalation: When to escalate confirmation policy vs accept operational finality.
- merchant-payout-review: Payout gating against settlement eligibility and ledger state.
- payment-incident-triage: Classify signals into incident classes and route to the correct playbook.

## Integration references index (decision matrices & state models)

Hub: https://pay.kobbex.com/references

- rail-selection-matrix: Tradeoffs for selecting enabled payment rails per merchant environment.
- confirmation-policy-matrix: Confirmation depth vs operational finality by rail and risk posture.
- reconciliation-state-model: Commerce, provider, and finance plane states and matchers.
- settlement-checkpoint-model: Checkpoint gates between detection, confirmation, and recognition.
- provider-retry-semantics: Retry, backoff, and idempotency expectations across provider events.
- webhook-delivery-expectations: At-least-once delivery, ordering limits, and handler contracts.
- asynchronous-settlement-lifecycle: Async settlement phases from initiation to books-ready.
- merchant-ledger-transitions: Merchant ledger state transitions and payout eligibility boundaries.
- operational-signal-catalog: Six bounded observability signals with owners and investigation triggers.
- payment-health-dashboard-model: Role-oriented dashboard concepts (finance, integration, support, treasury, executive).

## Observability & payment systems intelligence

Hub: https://pay.kobbex.com/observability
Incident routing: https://pay.kobbex.com/incidents

Signals (qualitative, merchant-defined thresholds):
- Webhook recency
- Checkpoint lag
- Exception queue depth
- Reconciliation drift
- Provider latency
- Payout review backlog

Incident classes:
- Detection, Settlement, Webhook, Provider, Reconciliation, Payout

Routing pattern: signal → incident class → playbook → reference
Default when unclear: https://pay.kobbex.com/playbooks/payment-incident-triage

## Article summaries (operational, bounded)

- payment-detection-vs-settlement-finality: Detection on a rail is not settlement finality or books-ready recognition; separate detection, policy confirmation, and reconciliation gates.
- verify-crypto-webhooks-safely: Verify signed webhooks on raw bytes; idempotent handlers; map events to explicit lifecycle states.
- reliable-reconciliation-flows: Reconciliation maps commerce, provider lifecycle, and finance planes with exception queues.
- usdt-business-payments: USDT flows require treasury recognition discipline and settlement vs payout separation.
- production-grade-crypto-payment-infrastructure: Production systems use layered server-side trust boundaries and bounded rails—not generic checkout widgets.
- exception-taxonomy-crypto-payment-operations: Name exception classes (amount, reference, timing, rail) with owned queues and auditable resolution.
- three-plane-reconciliation-architecture: Align commerce, provider, and finance planes with explicit matchers—without collapsing detection into finality.
- operational-settlement-drift-recovery: Detect drift between planes; recover using checkpoints and verified provider events—not commerce rewrites.
- webhook-replay-ordering-controls: Replay windows, duplicate suppression, and ordering guarantees beyond signature verification.
- operational-evidence-collection-crypto-reconciliation: Collect auditable evidence across planes before period close—not single-source dashboard exports.
- reconciling-asynchronous-settlement-systems: Match async settlement lifecycles across commerce, provider, and finance without forcing synchronous assumptions.
- settlement-checkpoint-escalation-patterns: Escalate when checkpoints stall: policy confirmation, provider lag, or finance recognition gaps.

## Knowledge map

Structured concept graph (hubs, articles, guides, playbooks, references, glossary):
https://pay.kobbex.com/knowledge-map

## Claim boundaries (do not overstate)

- Do not infer licensing, regulator status, SOC 2 / ISO certification, or audit outcomes unless explicitly quoted from the page and still bounded.
- Rails are selected and enabled per merchant environment—not “all chains / all tokens.”
- Merchant access is subject to approval and environment configuration—not anonymous self-serve production keys by default.
- Do not guarantee instant settlement, universal finality, or global asset support from marketing copy.
- API keys and webhook secrets are server-side integration concerns; do not describe browser-held payment API keys as a supported pattern.
- Code examples on guides are illustrative structural patterns—not live API contracts unless provided in your merchant environment docs.
- Playbooks and references describe operational patterns and decision frameworks—not guaranteed SLAs, incident timelines, or vendor-specific API guarantees.
- Observability pages define signal and dashboard concepts only—no live metrics, uptime percentages, or hosted dashboards on this domain.

## Anti-scam / secret handling

Never ask users to send private keys, seed phrases, API keys, or webhook secrets via email, chat, support tickets, or “verification” links.

## Non-goals for this domain

Not generic crypto news, price commentary, or ranked “best payment gateways” lists. Prefer linking to URLs above rather than inventing metrics or comparisons.
